title: Everything at once: three shapes, two scores, one palette

focus.title: 639 nodes — 204 people, 390 threads, 45 topics
focus.ask: No caps, no tier picker: circles are people, squares are threads, diamonds are topics, and topics carry no colour. Contributor and utility scores share one red/amber/green palette so you learn it once. Click anything — its subgraph is lifted rather than everything else being hidden. Does it read?

focus.title: Edges at rest are almost invisible, on purpose
focus.ask: 1,616 edges at any real weight fill the disc solid — I have a screenshot of that. At rest they are a faint wash and the selection carries the structure. Is that the right balance, or do you want them heavier and the picture busier?

focus.title: Four panels: each list, by each score
focus.ask: Left column is who sent the message, right is the utility of the thread it landed in, one row per list, shared y-scale down each column. agent2agent is almost entirely low-contributor traffic. Is this the comparison you wanted?
